issue.title: Bug:[FRR][bgpd] running tcpdump on a BGP-neighbor interface triggers a full route re-download

failure.body: ### Is it platform specific generic ### Importance or Severity High ### Description of the bug Running `tcpdump` on an interface that has BGP neighbors triggers an unnecessary full route re-download, even without fib suppression enabled. Opening the capture puts the interface in promiscuous mode, which makes the kernel emit a netlink link message; zebra forwards it as a duplicate ZEBRA_INTERFACE_UP (oper up→up) even though nothing changed, and bgpd then re-evaluates the BGP nexthop cache (BNC) and re-installs/re-advertises every route via that interface. On a router with thousands of routes via an uplink this is a full-RIB re-install per tcpdump; with `bgp suppress-fib-pending` it floods the offload-confirmation path and delays BGP advertisement by multiple seconds. This is a regression: it was fixed by PR #21805 ### Steps to Reproduce **Preconditions**: a SONiC switch running BGP with many routes via an uplink (e.g. a T1 with several thousand routes over an uplink PortChannel), bgp suppress-fib-pending enabled (makes the re-download trivially visible via the offload flag; the route re-download itself happens regardless). **_method 1:_** Run community test on t1 topology: `bgp/test_bgp_suppress_fib.py::test_bgp_update_relay_latency`, which recently merged in https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/23390. The test’s [tcpdump sniffer step ](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/c93b8c4f0e722e45c1ddf90c2f6fee98f5ebcef8/tests/bgp/test_bgp_suppress_fib.py#L1659)triggered a full-RIB re-installs (~8k routes), which caused the latency of seconds during offload confirmation (orchagent → ROUTE_TABLE_RESPONSE_CHANNEL → fpmsyncd). The test itself will fail sincethe latency added **_method 2:_** manual reproduction on switch with T2 neighbour **1.Find the uplink interface toward an upstream (T2) BGP neighbor:** ```bash show ip bgp summary | grep T2 # pick a T2 neighbor IP, e.g. show ip route # -> "directly connected, PortChannelXXX" (the uplink iface) ``` **2.Confirm steady state — zero routes pending offload:** ```bash sudo vtysh -c "show ip route json" | python3 -c \ 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print("not_offloaded=",sum(1 for p in d.values() for r in p if r.get("installed") and not r.get("offloaded")))' # expect: not_offloaded= 0 ``` **3.Watch the pending-offload count (terminal 1) and start a capture on the uplink (terminal 2):** ```bash # terminal 1 — watch: while true; do date +%H:%M:%S | tr -d '\n'; \ sudo vtysh -c "show ip route json" | python3 -c \ 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(" not_offloaded=",sum(1 for p in d.values() for r in p if r.get("installed") and not r.get("offloaded")))'; \ sleep 1; done # terminal 2 — trigger (replace with your uplink ifa sudo timeout 5 tcpdump -ni PortChannelXXX 'tcp port 179' ``` **4.Observe: the instant tcpdump opens the interface (promiscuous mode), not_offloaded jumps from 0 → ~full RIB (~7,500 on this box) and drains over ~10s — i.e. tcpdump alone re-downloaded . No clear bgp, no config change.** Corroborating logs: ```bash # duplicate link-up from promiscuous mode: sudo grep -E "entered promiscuous mode|updatePortOpe /var/log/syslog # -> "Port PortChannelXXX oper state set from up to up" (a no-op up->up) # the route re-install storm: sudo docker exec swss sh -c \ "grep ROUTE_TABLE /var/log/swss/swss.rec | grep '|SET|' | tail -3000 | grep -oE '[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]' | uniq -c | tail" # -> a SET burst of thousands/sec right after the tcpdump ``` ### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior **Actual:** Running `tcpdump` on a BGP-neighbor / uplink interface causes a duplicate interface up→up event and a full route re-download. Reproduced on FRR 10.5.4: `tcpdump -ni PortChannel102 'tcp port 179'` on an idle box drove installed-but-not-offloaded routes from 0 to ~7,500 (the whole RIB via that uplink), draining over ~10s — with no clear/config/topology change. Both entering and leaving promiscuous mode fired it: kernel: PortChannel102: entered promiscuous mode orchagent: updatePortOperStatus: Port PortChannel102 oper state set from up to up -> swss.rec ROUTE_TABLE |SET burst up to 5120/s (BGP routes via the uplinks) **Expected:** `tcpdump` / promiscuous mode is a passive, local monitoring operation that does not change reachability or topology — it must NOT trigger any route update or download. The pending-offload count should stay 0 and there should be no route re-install. (Control: the same tcpdump on a non-BGP interface, e.g. eth0, causes no route churn.) ### Relevant log output ```shell 1. not_offloaded curve (the effect — tcpdump alone re-downloads the RIB) not_offloaded=0 ← steady state not_offloaded=0 ← tcpdump opened here not_offloaded=7526 ← jumped: ~7.5k routes re-downloaded not_offloaded=6136 not_offloaded=7076 ← tcpdump closed (adds a 2nd wave) not_offloaded=6532 not_offloaded=1706 not_offloaded=387 not_offloaded=0 ← drained (~10s total) 2. syslog — the trigger (promiscuous → duplicate link-up → MTU re-set), on BOTH open and close # --- tcpdump OPEN --- .019 kernel: PortChannel102: entered promiscuous mode .019 kernel: Ethernet96: entered promiscuous mode (PC102 members) .019 kernel: Ethernet104: entered promiscuous mode .019 swss#portsyncd: onMsg: nlmsg type:16 key:Ethernet96 admin:1 oper:1 ... master:193 type:sx_netdev .019 swss#portsyncd: onMsg: nlmsg type:16 kr:1 ... type:team .022 swss#orchagent: updatePortOperStatus: Port PortChannel102 oper state set from up to up ← DUPLICATE up→up .024 swss#orchagent: setRouterIntfsMtu: Set102 MTU to 9100 # --- tcpdump CLOSE (5s later) — fires it AGAIN --- .019 kernel: PortChannel102: left promiscuous mode .019 kernel: Ethernet96/Ethernet104: left p .069 swss#orchagent: updatePortOperStatus: Port PortChannel102 oper state set from up to up ← DUPLICATE up→up .126 swss#orchagent: setRouterIntfsMtu: Set102 MTU to 9100 3. swss.rec — the route re-install storm ROUTE_TABLE |SET per second: 1146/s ← begins right after promiscuous-mode entry 1907/s 3072/s 2048/s 2048/s (tcpdump close adds more) 5120/s ← peak 5120/s 2059/s Sample re-installed routes (these are the T2-learned .046 ROUTE_TABLE:20c0:e658::/64 SET protocol:bgp nexthop:fc00::2,fc00::a,fc00::12,fc00::1a ifname:PortChannel102,105,108,111 .053 ROUTE_TABLE:/25 SET protocol:bgp nexthop:,,, ifname:PortChannel102,105,108,111 .301 ROUTE_TABLE:/25 SET protocol:bgp nexthop:,,, ifname:PortChannel102,105,108,111 .517 ROUTE_TABLE:::/64 SET protocol:bgp nexthop:fc00::2,fc00::a,fc00::12,fc00::1a ifname:PortChannel102,105,108,111 4. offload-confirm churn (fpmsyncd RESPONSE_CHANNEL received=322560 received=325632 received=350208 ← ~27.6k confirms pro ``` ### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport` ```shell ``` ### Attach files (if any) _No response_

resolution.title: [sonic-frr]: suppress full BGP route re-download when tcpdump toggles interface promiscuity
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it

Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/28026

On a BGP-enabled port or PortChannel, running `tcpdump` (or opening any `AF_PACKET` socket) toggles `IFF_PROMISC`. FRR 10.5.4 zebra does not filter a promiscuity-only netlink change in `zebra_if_dplane_ifp_handling`, so it emits a spurious `ZEBRA_INTERFACE_UP`. bgpd then re-evaluates every nexthop tracked via that interface and re-advertises/re-installs the full RIB (thousands of routes, ~10 s of control-plane churn). A routine packet capture on a production device should never trigger a routing storm.

Root cause: the netlink `ifi_change` mask carrying `IFF_PROMISC` (`0x100`) is not inspected before the interface is treated as having changed operational state.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

Add SONiC FRR patch `0115`, a backport of upstream [FRRouting/frr PR 20181](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/20181) (commit `257edcc948e0179c75933cdb862fe1ac4ac14085`, "zebra: Update promiscuity flag silently without route resets").

The patch plumbs the netlink `ifi_change` mask through the dplane (`dplane_ctx_set/get_ifp_change_flags`) and, in `zebra_if_dplane_ifp_handling`, skips the routing notification when promiscuity is the **only** changed flag (`change_flags == IFF_PROMISC`, exact match on the masked value). The interface flags are still updated, so `show interface` reflects the correct PROMISC state.

PR scope — patch-based, **no submodule pointer change**:
- `src/sonic-frr/patch/0115-zebra-Update-promiscuity-flag-silently-without-route.patch`
- `src/sonic-frr/patch/series`

Porting note: upstream's `frrtrace(... if_dplane_ifp_handling_new ...)` tracepoint does not exist on `frr-10.5.4` and is omitted; the suppression logic is otherwise verbatim. Upstream PR 20181 is not yet in a released `stable/10.5`, hence the SONiC patch.

#### How to verify it

- **Patch apply:** full series `0001`–`0115` applies cleanly on a pristine `frr-10.5.4` tree (0 rejects).
- **Compile:** `frr_10.5.4-sonic-0_amd64.deb` builds clean with the patch applied (and the `docker-fpm-frr` container assembles).
- **Functional (KVM t1-lag, cEOS neighbors, before/after container swap):** Trigger (both runs): `tcpdump -ni PortChannel102 'tcp port 179'` (open+close) on a LAG uplink. DUT had 24 BGP sessions Established, RIB ~12.8k.

  | Metric | BEFORE (unfixed FRR 10.5.4) | AFTER (patch 0115) |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | swss.rec `ROUTE_TABLE` ops | **25,512** | **0** |
  | bgpd `eval path` lines | 10,059 | 0 |
  | zebra `ZEBRA_INTERFACE_UP PortChannel102` | yes | no |
  | zebra `PROMISC-only update … no routing notification` (fix firing) | n/a | yes |
  | RIB ebgp routes (steady) | 6,427 | 6,427 |

BEFORE: the promisc toggle produced a spurious `ZEBRA_INTERFACE_UP`, bgpd re-evaluated the paths, and the full RIB was re-downloaded (25,512 `ROUTE_TABLE` ops). AFTER: the same toggle produced **zero** route ops, zero path re-evaluation, and no `ZEBRA_INTERFACE_UP`; `not_offloaded` stayed 0. `ip monitor` confirmed the netlink delta is `promiscuity` only (`ifi_change == IFF_PROMISC`, `0x100`), not allmulti.
- **sonic-mgmt:** `bgp/test_bgp_suppress_fib.py::test_bgp_update_relay_latency` → **PASS**.

#### Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)

- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [ ] 202605

#### Tested branch (Please provide the tested image version)

- [x] master — base image `sonic-vs` build `1145536` (master, 2026-06-22) with the patched `docker-fpm-frr` container swapped in.

#### Description for the changelog

[sonic-frr] zebra: suppress full BGP route re-download on interface promiscuity-only changes (tcpdump toggling `IFF_PROMISC`).

N/A — no CONFIG_DB schema or YANG changes.
